text: Feeding rapamycin to adult *Drosophila melanogaster* extends life span, reproducing the longevity seen in some TOR mutants. The target of rapamycin (TOR) pathway is a major nutrient-sensing pathway whose genetic downregulation increases life span in evolutionarily diverse organisms, including mammals; TOR kinase is its central component and rapamycin is a highly specific, well-described inhibitory drug approved for human use. Rapamycin-induced longevity was associated with increased resistance to both starvation and paraquat. Mechanistic analysis showed rapamycin extended life span specifically through the TORC1 branch of the TOR pathway, via alterations to both autophagy and translation. Rapamycin also increased life span of weak insulin/Igf signaling (IIS) pathway mutants and of flies whose life span was maximized by dietary restriction, indicating additional mechanisms.
